purpose: Test whether discarding the inherited AdamW history contributes to continued-training regression
trigger: All three recovery screens failed. Saved raw/EMA weights and all 469 moment tensors passed the CPU audit; raw weights alone scored worse than final EMA.
comparison: Two new matched seed-7919 runs. Both start from saved raw model weights and saved EMA, with beta=(0.9,0.95), per-protein latent loss, the original 1024-protein pool, 500 updates, pilot LR 1e-5 with 100-step warmup/cosine decay and EMA decay 0.99. Both use unchanged single-tensor AdamW and all-block recomputation. Only restored versus fresh optimizer history differs.
treatment: Restore exp_avg, exp_avg_sq and per-parameter step counters (63235). Preserve the new experiment's LR schedule and optimizer kernel. The comparison isolates complete optimizer history, not moments independently of their bias-correction counters.
beta_rationale: Both new arms use the original beta2=0.95 so historical moments are interpreted with their original decay. These new arms do not reuse the EMA-initialized pilot as their causal control.
controls: Revalidate saved ordering, coverage, shapes, finiteness and counters; require four actual FP16-versus-FP32 parameter-gradient controls in each run. Require identical logged input IDs, flow RNG, batch shapes, updates and all other settings between arms. Full strict-FP32 evaluation and unchanged shape controls on 626 targets with three samples, 25 steps, CFG 2.
followup: Replicate this pair for seeds 7920/7921 only if restored history improves TM at least 0.002 over fresh history and reaches untouched final-EMA TM 0.5682384930777423, with complete valid evaluation. Report lDDT and geometry separately. No accuracy promotion until the existing +0.01, uncertainty and replication gates and independent confirmation are met.
limitations: This resets the original LR schedule and data stream; missing CUDA RNG prevents exact replay. It tests a bounded state-restored continuation, not an exact resumption or the general benefit of longer training.
